content.text:
Ca2VWO6 (mp-1296431) accounts for all the strong peaks, so I report it alone.

1. **Ca2VWO6 fits.** I calculated d-spacings from its cell (a = 5.50, b = 5.68, c = 7.87 Å) and converted them with Cu Kα.
   - (011) and (101) come out near 19.3° and 19.7°. The pattern has a doublet at 19.2° and 19.6°.
   - (110) and (002) come out near 22.5–22.6°. The pattern has a strong peak at about 22.6°.
   - (020), (112) and (200) come out near 31.5°, 32.1° and 32.5°. The pattern has its strongest peak at about 32.3°, with neighbours near 31.25° and 33°.
   - (013) comes out near 37.7°, inside the broad feature at 37–38°.

2. **YbGaO3 fits less well.** Its main reflections fall at about 22.9°, 24.0°, 31.8° and 33.4°. That puts the strongest line away from 32.3°, and the pattern has no peak at 24°.

3. **The spinels and Ba2SmMoO6 do not fit.** LiFe3O4 and MgNi2O4 would put their main peaks near 30° and 35.5°. Ba2SmMoO6 would put its main peak near 29.7°. The pattern shows none of these.

4. **The other candidates were not checked line by line.** These are SmBiO4, Rb2Hf2O5, CsO2 and MnO2. With Ca2VWO6 covering the strong peaks, I see no need for a second phase. Not having ruled these four out is the main reason confidence is below 0.9.
